study_material.title: Chain Rule / Variation - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Variation problems ask how one quantity changes when related quantities change - more men means fewer days, more speed means less time. The chain rule (unitary method) turns these into one-line proportions, and is the backbone of time-and-work and pipes-and-cisterns problems.
learning_objectives: Distinguish direct from inverse variation at a glance
Apply the man-days (M1 D1 H1 = M2 D2 H2 style) equation
Solve combined variation with several changing quantities

concepts.heading: 1. Direct Variation
concepts.body: x and y vary directly if x/y is constant: more computers, more cost. Then x1/x2 = y1/y2. Examples: cost vs quantity, distance vs time at fixed speed, work done vs number of identical workers.

concepts.heading: 2. Inverse Variation
concepts.body: x and y vary inversely if xy is constant: more workers, fewer days. Then x1/x2 = y2/y1. Examples: speed vs time for fixed distance, men vs days for fixed work, pipes vs filling time.

concepts.heading: 3. The Work Equation
concepts.body: For jobs measured in man-hours: (M1 x D1 x H1) / W1 = (M2 x D2 x H2) / W2, where M = men, D = days, H = hours per day, W = amount of work. With equal work it reduces to M1 D1 H1 = M2 D2 H2. Set up the equation, plug in knowns, solve the single unknown.

concepts.heading: 4. Combined Variation
concepts.body: If x varies directly with y and inversely with z, then x = k(y/z), so x1/x2 = (y1/y2) x (z2/z1). Write each factor as 'does more of this quantity increase or decrease the answer?' and orient the fraction accordingly - this sanity check prevents most errors.

concepts.heading: 5. Provisions Problems
concepts.body: Food for M men lasting D days = MD man-days of provisions. If people leave or join after d days, compute remaining man-days = M(D - d), then divide by the new headcount to get remaining days.

formulas: M1 D1 H1 / W1 = M2 D2 H2 / W2
Remaining provisions (man-days) = headcount x days left
shortcut_methods: Ask 'more or less?' for each changing quantity and multiply correction fractions onto the base value
Keep one unknown; convert everything else to numbers first
For provisions: always convert to man-days immediately
common_mistakes: Inverting the wrong fraction in inverse variation
Ignoring hours-per-day when both days and daily hours change
Forgetting that work amount can change too (walls of different lengths)
study_material.summary: Identify each quantity as direct or inverse, write the chain of correction fractions, and compute. The man-days equation covers nearly every variant.
quick_revision_notes: Direct: ratio same way; Inverse: ratio flips
M1 D1 H1 = M2 D2 H2 for equal work
x directly with y, inversely with z: x = ky/z

solved_examples.question: 15 men can build a wall in 20 days. How long will 25 men take?
solved_examples.step_by_step: Men and days vary inversely: 15 x 20 = 25 x D, so D = 300/25 = 12 days.

solved_examples.question: If 5 kg of rice costs Rs. 240, what do 8 kg cost?
10 men working 6 hours a day finish a job in 18 days. In how many days will 15 men working 8 hours a day finish it?
y varies inversely as x, and y = 9 when x = 4. Find y when x = 6.
A garrison of 200 men has provisions for 45 days. After 15 days, 50 men leave. How long will the remaining food last the rest?
solved_examples.step_by_step: Remaining provisions = 200 x 30 = 6000 man-days. Remaining men = 150. Days = 6000/150 = 40.
solved_examples.shortcut: 30 days' food for 200 men stretches by factor 200/150 = 4/3: 30 x 4/3 = 40.

practice_questions.question: 36 men can eat a stock of food in 30 days. How long will the same stock last 27 men?
practice_questions.explanation: 36 x 30 = 27 x D, so D = 40 days.

practice_questions.question: A car covers 240 km in 4 hours. At the same speed, how long for 360 km?
8 identical pumps empty a tank in 6 hours. How long would 12 such pumps take?
practice_questions.explanation: 8 x 6 = 12 x t, so t = 4 hours.

practice_questions.question: A 20 m rope weighs 4 kg. What does a 35 m rope of the same kind weigh?
practice_questions.explanation: Weight per metre = 0.2 kg; 35 x 0.2 = 7 kg.

practice_questions.question: 12 workers working 5 days earn Rs. 6,000. How much will 8 workers earn in 7 days at the same rate?
practice_questions.explanation: Wages scale with worker-days: 6000 x (8x7)/(12x5) = 6000 x 56/60 = 5,600.

practice_questions.question: x varies as the square of y. When y doubles, x becomes:
practice_questions.explanation: x = ky^2, so doubling y multiplies x by 2^2 = 4.

practice_questions.question: 20 cows graze a field in 12 days. How long would 15 cows take on the same field?
practice_questions.explanation: 20 x 12 = 15 x D, so D = 16 days.

practice_questions.question: If x varies directly as y, and x = 6 when y = 8, find x when y = 20.
9 workers working 6 hours a day complete a job in 10 days. How many days will 12 workers working 5 hours a day need?
8 kg of cotton makes 40 m of cloth. How much cotton is needed for 100 m of the same cloth?
practice_questions.explanation: Cotton per metre = 0.2 kg; 100 x 0.2 = 20 kg.

topic_test.title: Chain Rule / Variation - Topic Test
instructions: +1 for correct, -0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
Decide direct vs inverse for each quantity before computing.

questions.question: 14 men can do a job in 18 days. How many days will 21 men take?
6 machines produce a batch in 4 hours. How long would 8 machines take?
If 12 notebooks cost Rs. 300, what do 20 notebooks cost?
y varies inversely as x. If y = 12 when x = 5, find x when y = 20.
A contractor employs 30 men to finish a road in 40 days. After 10 days he finds only 1/5 of the road built. How many extra men (working at the same rate) does he need to finish on time?
questions.explanation: 1/5 work took 300 man-days, so full road = 1500. Remaining 4/5 = 1200 man-days in 30 days needs 40 men - 10 extra.

questions.question: A wheel makes 500 revolutions to cover 1 km. How many revolutions to cover 2.5 km?
Food lasts 20 people for 30 days. If 5 more people join at the start, how long does it last?
If 5 men or 8 boys can do a job in 24 days, how long will 10 men and 4 boys take?
questions.explanation: 1 man = 8/5 boys, so 10 men + 4 boys = 16 + 4 = 20 boy-units. 8 boys x 24 days = 192 boy-days; 192/20 = 9.6 days.

questions.question: x varies directly as y and inversely as z. When y = 10 and z = 5, x = 8. Find x when y = 15 and z = 6.
A fort had provisions for 150 men for 45 days. After 10 days, 25 men left. How long will the remaining food last?
questions.explanation: Remaining = 150 x 35 = 5250 man-days for 125 men: 5250/125 = 42 days.
